methodology: The study evaluated the textile potential of five underexplored Agave varieties through combined analyses of extraction behaviour, microstructure, and single-fibre mechanical performance. Fibre samples were extracted from basal, middle, and upper leaf sections and characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and single-fibre tensile testing under controlled conditions.
research_objective: To evaluate the textile potential of five Agave varieties and determine which species selection and leaf position management are key parameters for optimising Agave fibre performance in textile applications.

key_findings.finding: Species selection and leaf position management are key parameters for optimising Agave fibre performance in textile applications.

Appropriate fibre selection and blending strategies are required to control intra-leaf variability and produce homogeneous yarns from Agave fibres, supporting their potential use as sustainable bio-based textile resources.
Agave fibers offer competitive specific mechanical properties compared to other lignocellulosic fibers such as flax, hemp, or jute while benefiting from lower cultivation constraints.

Agave plants are well adapted to arid and semi-arid environments requiring limited water input, minimal fertilization, and low agrochemical usage compared to cotton cultivation which is associated with high water consumption and intensive agricultural inputs leading to higher production costs and environmental burdens.
The study investigates five lesser-studied Agave varieties and aims to provide a systematic evaluation of extraction behavior, microstructural characteristics, and single-fiber mechanical properties.
The objective is to clarify the structural origins of performance differences and identify agave fibers suitable for sustainable textile applications.
Extraction conditions were kept consistent for all samples to ensure comparability between Agave varieties.
